methodology.read_method: Numbered full-file display in bounded chunks without truncation; inclusive spans recorded per file. Before display, bytes were checked against ledger hashes; final primary digest checks cover all 25 paths after all review.

classification.concrete_test_source_finding: An observable oracle weakness with a concrete incorrect result the cited assertions do not reject; not a confirmed production bug.
classification.coverage_limitation: A scenario, independence check or research inference not established by the cited cases; no repository-wide absence claim.

methodology.statistical_basis: Complete census of the 25 selected source files, not sampled test outcomes. Read counts are exact descriptive counts. No tests, mutations, benchmarks or model experiments ran; confidence intervals, significance, failure probabilities and release readiness are not estimable and are not asserted.
assumptions: Source assertions are interpreted statically; imported helper behavior and production code were not inspected.
Source comments/test names do not constitute execution evidence.
Suggested improvements are recommendations only; no test or production edits were made.

summary.coverage_claim: All listed source lines reviewed at pinned hashes; this is not code-execution coverage or a test pass-rate claim.

findings.title: Combined-loss backward does not prove each geometry regularizer is differentiable
findings.observation: The test checks collision, boundary and box values are positive, then backpropagates only result['loss'] and requires finite position gradients.
findings.undetected_regression: A detached positive constant for one or all optional regularizers can satisfy these assertions while another active loss supplies the position gradient. A zero gradient also satisfies isfinite.
findings.claim_impact: This case cannot substantiate that each optional geometry penalty contributes a useful training gradient.
findings.suggested_oracle: Use separate nondegenerate fixtures with other loss terms disabled; differentiate each regularizer and require finite nonzero gradients with an analytically expected direction.
findings.confidence: Direct static assertion evidence; no production defect or executed mutation established.

findings.title: Shuffle test loses the identity of the chair with invalid position labels
findings.observation: Both chairs share description/category. The original dictionary is keyed by description, geometry equality explicitly excludes chairs, and the invalid-mask check only verifies that exactly one chair is invalid.
findings.undetected_regression: Moving the invalid position mask from chair_b to chair_a during shuffling, or mismatching the two chair geometries with masks, preserves the asserted category, group membership and invalid count.
findings.claim_impact: Incorrect supervision eligibility can survive this regression test and affect geometry losses and matching metrics.
findings.suggested_oracle: Track each original target and its full validity tuple through the ID permutation, using distinct target coordinates as a test-only identity witness; verify both chairs, not only category/count.
findings.confidence: Direct static assertion evidence; production behavior not inspected.

findings.title: Five-room handoff oracle checks child height but not parent footprint containment
findings.observation: For on_object placements the loop verifies parent metadata and either top height or an interior z interval. It does not compare the child's x/y footprint with its parent, nor its top with an interior support volume; only the bathroom is subsequently assembled.
findings.undetected_regression: An on_object child horizontally outside its parent at the accepted z satisfies this loop's placement assertions. An interior child can also extend above the parent while its bottom remains inside the accepted interval.
findings.claim_impact: The 313-object handoff checks do not by themselves certify physical support or containment across the five rooms.
findings.suggested_oracle: Independently check oriented child-footprint containment/contact against the declared parent's support surface, and for interior placements check full vertical bounds. Include deliberately displaced and over-tall children.
findings.confidence: Direct static assertion evidence; no claim that the current decoder produces these failures.

findings.title: Hungarian shifted-error assertion accepts invalid negative distance metrics
findings.observation: The Hungarian branch requires only mean <= 0.10 + 1e-9. The fixed-ID branch checks an exact approximately 0.10 error.
findings.undetected_regression: Any negative mean passes the Hungarian inequality; an incorrectly zero-valued matched error also is not challenged by this assertion.
findings.claim_impact: This shifted-prediction case supplies no independent nonzero matching-error oracle for research metrics.
findings.suggested_oracle: Add a small known-cost exchangeable fixture with an independently enumerated optimal assignment and a strictly positive expected mean; assert finite nonnegative errors in this branch.
findings.confidence: Direct static assertion evidence; no executed negative mutation or production failure.

findings.title: The rotated-constraint identity test asserts endpoint membership, not source identity.
findings.observation: The only output checks are type == 'near' and membership of object_id and target_id in the condition ID set.
findings.undetected_regression: Both endpoints can be the same existing ID. A changed distance threshold is also unexamined.
findings.claim_impact: A constraint can bind the wrong source objects while the migration test appears to preserve relations.
findings.suggested_oracle: Derive expected endpoints from source identity and assert the complete converted constraint, including its distance.
findings.confidence: Direct static assertion evidence from the delegated full-file review; no production defect or executed mutation established.

findings.title: The precise-target test does not bind geometry to source identity.
findings.observation: Its numeric target oracle only requires 1.1234 to appear among first size components. It does not compare complete size, position, or yaw per source object.
findings.undetected_regression: Swapping the two complete geometry records between their object identities preserves the checked scalar membership. Changes to the unchecked coordinates and yaw also leave that assertion unchanged.
findings.claim_impact: Geometry identity/order corruption can evade the legacy migration oracle and compromise reference supervision.
findings.suggested_oracle: Use target_source_ids to compare every target's size, bottom center, and yaw with the corresponding fixture object.
findings.confidence: Direct static assertion evidence from the delegated full-file review; no production defect or executed mutation established.

findings.title: The degenerate-size preservation oracle compares against the parent after the call.
findings.observation: No pre-call snapshot is retained. Line 140 compares row.target with parent.target, while the original size is checked only in qualification_changes.value_m.
findings.undetected_regression: Changing both returned and parent target sizes to another degenerate size, while recording the original [1.4, 0.0029, 0.75] in the journal, satisfies these equality and journal assertions.
findings.claim_impact: Clamping or rewriting evidence can masquerade as qualification without mutation being detected by this case.
findings.suggested_oracle: Snapshot the parent before qualification, then compare both the parent and returned target against that snapshot.
findings.confidence: Direct static assertion evidence from the delegated full-file review; no production defect or executed mutation established.

findings.title: Two facing-qualification tests check remaining constraint count without checking constraint identity.
findings.observation: The fixture contains faces and against_wall. Both tests assert only that one constraint remains.
findings.undetected_regression: Retaining faces while removing against_wall satisfies these assertions, including the target-order case.
findings.claim_impact: Evidence qualification can remove a valid spatial relation while retaining an unsupported facing relation.
findings.suggested_oracle: Assert that the retained list is exactly the original against_wall constraint and that omission provenance identifies faces.
findings.confidence: Direct static assertion evidence from the delegated full-file review; no production defect or executed mutation established.

findings.title: The implementation-provenance test checks a path key without checking its digest.
findings.observation: Line 134 only tests membership of the resolved legacy_bridge path in implementation_sha256.
findings.undetected_regression: That key can contain an empty, stale, or all-zero digest without failing the assertion.
findings.claim_impact: Presence of a provenance entry alone cannot substantiate binding research data to the actual conversion implementation.
findings.suggested_oracle: Compare the recorded value with an independently computed file digest when this test is executed.
findings.confidence: Direct static assertion evidence from the delegated full-file review; no production defect or executed mutation established.

coverage_limitations.title: Real distributed training verifies activity rather than numeric update equivalence
coverage_limitations.limitation: Real Gloo cases assert update counts, positive head gradients and changed parameter-tensor counts; final rank artifacts are only checked for existence. The separate global-count test mocks collectives. Neither provides an independent rank-to-rank and single-process parameter/gradient comparison in these files.
coverage_limitations.implication: Incorrect global normalization or rank divergence can satisfy the activity observations; this is an untested numerical-equivalence claim, not a detected training bug.
coverage_limitations.recommended_follow_up: Compare full resulting tensors on both ranks to a deterministic single-process update on the same active labels, including uneven per-rank counts and empty accumulation windows.

coverage_limitations.title: Unequal-population metric pooling lacks a discriminating numerical oracle in the reviewed evaluation cases
coverage_limitations.limitation: Exact evaluation cases largely use zero/common errors or equal-sized rows; term logging uses equal per-add counts. These examples do not distinguish pooled per-object errors from a mean of row/source means when valid counts and errors both differ. The explicitly named mean-of-batches selection contract is not assumed to be a bug.
coverage_limitations.implication: These cases alone do not establish correct aggregation under heterogeneous source supervision.
coverage_limitations.recommended_follow_up: Use two sources/rows with unequal valid counts and unequal known errors; independently compute the intended global and per-source means and zero-label behavior. Assert selection weighting according to its documented contract.

coverage_limitations.title: Several real-data and provenance checks are conditional on local assets
coverage_limitations.limitation: Real-row coverage can skip without an external disk/qualifying row; LLM baseline history and train-demo checks can skip without their commit/dataset; the context-length case can skip without the cached tokenizer. RoomGenBench geometry tests require an external reference checkout. Fixtures and external assets were not opened in this audit.
coverage_limitations.implication: Source presence/full reading does not establish that any conditional case ran or that the local assets match research data; no observed skip count is reported.
coverage_limitations.recommended_follow_up: In a separately authorized execution audit, record asset fingerprints and explicit passed/skipped outcomes for each conditional gate.

coverage_limitations.title: Tiny-model, mocked-answer and synthetic-head cases do not measure research generalization or physical model quality
coverage_limitations.limitation: The train/eval smoke test changes provenance but retains the same geometry; structured answers are generated from labels or a relay stand-in; benchmark layouts use seeded synthetic heads; validation runs use tiny models.
coverage_limitations.implication: These are useful plumbing/oracle checks, but furnish no held-out quality, learned-model comparison, effect size, uncertainty interval or release-readiness estimate.
coverage_limitations.recommended_follow_up: Keep these regression tests, and substantiate research claims with separately authorized held-out experiments, dataset identity checks, repeated seeds and uncertainty appropriate to the sampling unit.

coverage_limitations.title: A low collapse score explicitly does not certify room containment
coverage_limitations.limitation: The test intentionally asserts two out-of-room objects with collapse_score == 0; the checked score combines overlap and central-quarter fractions.
coverage_limitations.implication: Interpreting that scalar alone as layout physical validity would exceed the tested contract. This is an explicit metric limitation, not an implementation defect.
coverage_limitations.recommended_follow_up: Report out-of-room/validator status alongside collapse score and test any research-facing summary that presents them together.

coverage_limitations.title: Rotated-box boundary discrimination is absent from the minimal-data fixture
coverage_limitations.limitation: The OBB boundary test uses yaw zero. It checks box extent rather than center-only containment, but does not distinguish rotated-corner containment from an axis-aligned calculation that ignores yaw.
coverage_limitations.implication: This specific oracle/scenario is not established by the cited test cases; absence elsewhere is not claimed.
coverage_limitations.recommended_follow_up: An anisotropic, rotated box whose containment differs when yaw is ignored.

coverage_limitations.title: Review manifest event counts are not distinguished from affected-row counts
coverage_limitations.limitation: Each affected row contains one omitted face or one floor-conflicting object. Event counts therefore equal affected-row counts in every asserted aggregate.
coverage_limitations.implication: This specific oracle/scenario is not established by the cited test cases; absence elsewhere is not claimed.
coverage_limitations.recommended_follow_up: Multiple omitted constraints and multiple floor-conflicting objects in one row, producing distinct event and row totals.

coverage_limitations.title: Large-inventory fixture is not an identity/alignment stress case
coverage_limitations.limitation: The 623-object fixture repeats one geometry record and uniform masks. Assertions check condition length and slot count, without establishing per-object label/mask alignment.
coverage_limitations.implication: This specific oracle/scenario is not established by the cited test cases; absence elsewhere is not claimed.
coverage_limitations.recommended_follow_up: Distinct geometry and heterogeneous masks near and beyond the usual object budget, with exact source-to-target-to-batch correspondence.

coverage_limitations.title: House-level split exclusion is not distinguished from group-level exclusion
coverage_limitations.limitation: Cross-split leakage fixtures set house_id, group, and raw group to the same shared value. They do not distinguish enforcement of house identity from enforcement of group identity alone.
coverage_limitations.implication: This specific oracle/scenario is not established by the cited test cases; absence elsewhere is not claimed.
coverage_limitations.recommended_follow_up: Distinct groups in different splits sharing one house_id.

coverage_limitations.title: Named IR-duplication coverage has no duplicated IR-record fixture
coverage_limitations.limitation: The test name includes IR duplication, but the body exercises cross-split groups and duplicate JSON keys only; it never duplicates an IR record.
coverage_limitations.implication: This specific oracle/scenario is not established by the cited test cases; absence elsewhere is not claimed.
coverage_limitations.recommended_follow_up: Repeated IR identity under an updated valid source seal, so duplicate detection is exercised independently of hash rejection.

coverage_limitations.title: Reviewed-build expectations reuse the same qualification function
coverage_limitations.limitation: The build test generates expected rows by calling review_sample again. This establishes agreement with that function, not an independent row-transformation oracle. Separate unit tests do assert preservation for their fixtures.
coverage_limitations.implication: This specific oracle/scenario is not established by the cited test cases; absence elsewhere is not claimed.
coverage_limitations.recommended_follow_up: An independently specified expected build row containing distinguishable geometry, masks, retained constraints, and omitted constraints.

files.coverage_limitations: Checks changed-tensor counts and positive gradients, without comparing resulting parameter values between ranks or against an independent single-process globally normalized update.
